rows.note: This is the all-purpose everyday choice for someone who tends to talk a lot, without necessarily judging them negatively.

example.english: They’re really talkative—you can chat with them all evening even when you first meet.
example.traditional: 佢真係好多嘢講，第一次見面都可以同你傾成晚。
example.jyutping: keoi5 zan1 hai6 hou2 do1 je5 gong2 dai6 jat1 ci3 gin3 min6 dou1 ho2 ji5 tung4 nei5 king1 sing4 maan5

rows.note: Use this when stressing that someone talks too much or cannot keep a secret, often with mild disapproval.

example.english: Don’t be so talkative; you can’t go around telling people about this.
example.traditional: 你唔好咁口多，呢件事唔可以周圍講。
example.jyutping: nei5 m4 hou2 gam3 hau2 do1 ni1 gin6 si6 m4 ho2 ji5 zau1 wai4 gong2

rows.note: Use this when the person is talkative in a tiresome, repetitive, or long-winded way.

example.english: My uncle gets really talkative and long-winded whenever he starts talking about that film.
example.traditional: 阿叔一講起嗰套戲就好長氣。
example.jyutping: aa3 suk1 jat1 gong2 hei2 go2 tou3 hei3 zau6 hou2 coeng4 hei3

rows.note: Use this for someone who is pleasantly sociable and good at keeping a conversation going, especially in a positive description.
